gen-gf-sofia-fs-neco: Neco is a serif whose strokes swell gently from hairline to stem. Under Sofia's ballpoint-pen heading it gives a longer read some dignity, though it is happiest in small doses.
gen-gf-sofia-fs-plein: Sofia looks like a laser cutting one width through a sheet, loose and friendly in its curves. And Plein, a plain sans with a clear channel leading into each round letter, stays comfortable in small doses.
gen-gf-sofia-fs-recia: Bold handwritten letters with no thick or thin strokes make Sofia feel like a marker in a relaxed hand. Recia is the quiet counterpart, a text serif whose light modulation only shows up on close inspection, which suits a handful of lines.
gen-gf-sofia-fs-rowan: Loose, chunky, and friendly, Sofia has crossbars as fat as its stems. But Rowan, a literary serif with thin strokes about half the weight of its thick ones, suits brief copy, while Sofia earns its keep big and short.
gen-gf-sofia-fs-spline-sans: Every stroke in Sofia's w is the same weight, giving the heading a hand-drawn, ballpoint feel. Spline Sans adds wide gaps between curve ends and stems.
gen-gf-sofia-fs-synonym: Synonym reads like a plain stripe of constant ink, dependable and clean. Sofia is the one with hand-drawn warmth and generous curves, while the sans quietly does the work, best in small doses.
gen-gf-sofia-outfit: Sofia leads with hand-drawn warmth and generous openings, while Outfit bends its curves like cable that finishes before it closes. Make the heading small and the charm fades.
gen-gf-sofia-plus-jakarta-sans: Loose hand-drawn charm, then crisp lines. And Plus Jakarta Sans, monoline with curve endings kept well apart, lets Sofia's relaxed heading breathe above a handful of lines.
gen-gf-sofia-sora: Sora is a precise, geometric sans-serif whose curves turn corners with no pressure swell, so its c and s stay widely parted. Sofia's heading can go large, but Sora is better for brief copy.
gen-gf-sofia-space-grotesk: Relaxed is the mood Sofia sets, with a hand-drawn w that never thickens or thins and curves left open. Space Grotesk answers with geometric counters, and it is not meant for long paragraphs.
